<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-definite-pair-geometry** [claim](#stmt-lem-definite-pair) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-definite-pair): Normalize the pair algebraically, use the decomposable complex volume kernel, and compare invariant positive cones. -> Associated almost-complex structure, trivial canonical line, taming equivalence and common Lagrangian planes.
- **step-topological-restrictions** [claim](#stmt-prop-topology) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-topology): Combine the symplectic Chern-class bound, characteristic-number identities, spin divisibility and even unimodular lattice classification. -> Betti-number and intersection-lattice alternatives.
- **step-coefficient-sphere-degree** [claim](#stmt-lem-twistor-degree) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-twistor-degree): Compare coefficient normals through a positive Gram matrix and identify closed anti-invariant forms with the harmonic basis. -> Smooth coefficient sphere with the required twistor degree and anti-invariant kernel.
- **step-equal-square-integrability** [claim](#stmt-lem-complex-symplectic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-complex-symplectic): Use closedness and Cartan's formula to prove involutivity, then identify the constant-norm holomorphic volume connection. -> Integrable complex structure and, with the third form, a parallel hyperkähler triple.
- **step-separate-positive-cones** [claim](#stmt-lem-current-separators) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-current-separators): Separate the positive cone from the invariant closed subspace or prescribed affine class, then represent the positive functional by complex-line measures. -> Normalized positive separator with the appropriate annihilation property.
- **step-closed-anti-invariant-lift** [claim](#stmt-lem-closed-lift) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-closed-lift): Invert the projected elliptic operator off its harmonic kernel and retain the kernel projection; apply the adjoint correction to the separator. -> Closed lift and closed cohomologically trivial corrected current, with smooth family dependence at constant kernel rank.
- **step-radial-operator-control** [claim](#stmt-lem-current-radial-operator) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-current-radial-operator): Split local Fourier control from off-diagonal dyadic shells and use the order-zero kernel bound. -> Uniform radial output bounds and control away from the center.
- **step-quadratic-current-mass** [claim](#stmt-lem-quadratic-mass) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-quadratic-mass): Test annihilation with cut-off logarithmic and square-root potentials, absorbing varying-structure and lift errors. -> Uniform quadratic trace growth.
- **step-resolvent-transport-kernel** [claim](#stmt-lem-current-kernel) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-current-kernel): Integrate a heat-kernel parametrix against the resolvent gamma weight and separate leading transport from the remainder. -> Positive scalar kernel with diagonal and decay bounds and a smaller transport error.
- **step-positive-current-pairings** [claim](#stmt-lem-current-positive-pairing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-current-positive-pairing): Expand the complex-line starred pairing algebraically and estimate kernel errors using quadratic mass. -> Angular lower bound and smoothed subcurrent norm control.
- **step-projection-leakage-control** [claim](#stmt-lem-current-commutator) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-current-commutator): Expand the commutator of the inverse smoothing polynomial with the bundle projection and use spectral Sobolev estimates. -> Small projection leakage and bounded mixed pairings.
- **step-angular-energy** [claim](#stmt-prop-angular-energy) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-angular-energy): Apply the smoothed topological square identity, complete the correction-norm square, then approximate the correction by smooth anti-invariant forms. -> Square-integrable correction, angular energy control and uniform mixed-pairing vanishing.
- **step-density-existence** [claim](#stmt-lem-density-existence) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-density-existence): Use frozen radial comparison, an almost-monotone mass ratio and differentiation relative to smooth volume. -> Bounded quadratic density everywhere and its volume-almost-everywhere vanishing.
- **step-planar-tangent-classification** [claim](#stmt-lem-density-planar-tangents) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-density-planar-tangents): Differentiate the current matrix, rescale closedness, exclude full-rank translation invariance, and identify the remaining plane measure. -> Single complex-line directions and unique planar tangent measures almost everywhere on the positive-density set.
- **step-integrated-transverse-decay** [claim](#stmt-cor-density-transverse) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-density-transverse): Pass to planar tangents at positive density and use vanishing mass ratios at zero density, followed by dominated convergence. -> Integrated transverse displacement decays beyond the quadratic scale.
- **step-closed-density-weights** [claim](#stmt-prop-density-weights) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-density-weights): Smooth the density, apply the closed-current product rule, control correction and tangential derivatives, then pass to fixed smooth weights and bounded thresholds. -> Closed smooth density weights, positive-density restriction and normalized threshold currents.
- **step-diffuse-error-vanishing** [claim](#stmt-lem-density-diffuse-error) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-density-diffuse-error): Use summable dyadic-shell bounds and dominated convergence at zero-density centers. -> Diffuse kernel error tends to zero in the required pairing.
- **step-taming-to-compatibility** [claim](#stmt-thm-tamed-compatible) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-density-diffuse-error-2): Pair the cohomologically trivial corrected separator with its diffuse correction, force the correction to vanish, and contradict strict taming. -> Existence of a compatible symplectic form without a prescribed class.
- **step-diffuse-square** [claim](#stmt-lem-density-diffuse-square) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-density-diffuse-square): Identify the diffuse self-pairing with its cohomological square and send the negative kernel error to zero. -> Nonnegative diffuse cohomological square.
- **step-integral-threshold-curves** [claim](#stmt-lem-density-integral-thresholds) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-density-integral-thresholds): Use positive finite densities for rectifiability, normalize multiplicity, check closedness, then apply almost-complex integral-cycle regularity after compatibility is established. -> Integral threshold cycles represented by finite positive curve sums and the layer-cake current identity.
- **step-prescribed-taming-cone** [claim](#stmt-thm-taming-cone) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-density-integral-thresholds-2): Split the class separator into diffuse and curve-threshold parts; use Lorentzian positivity on the former and the curve hypothesis on the latter. -> A smooth closed tamer in the specified class.
- **step-compatible-coefficient-family** [claim](#stmt-lem-compatible-family) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-compatible-family): Use the explicit constant-rank anti-invariant kernel, smooth closed lifts, local compatible corrections and a parameter partition of unity. -> Smooth compatible family with positive degree-one projected periods.
- **step-varying-taubes-incidence** [claim](#stmt-lem-families-taubes-compactness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rem-families-period-stability): Obtain uniform monopole estimates and support convergence, build relative integer assignments, retain incidences through disk deformations, and recognize positive limiting curves. -> Finite positive limiting configuration of the required real class, retaining zeros and excluding them uniformly in the zero-class case.
- **step-spherical-wall-crossing** [claim](#stmt-lem-families-wall-crossing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-families-wall-crossing): Compute the reducible-link projective pushforward with based-gauge normalization and identify the winding degree of the family wall section. -> Critical spherical chamber difference and vanishing constant-family evaluation.
- **step-evaluation-line** [claim](#stmt-lem-families-evaluation-line) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-families-evaluation-line): Compute the first eigenline's sphere Chern degree, include it in the evaluation line, and use fixed-parameter compactness to return from generic perturbations to exact incidence. -> Evaluation identity and exact first-component zeros when its pairing is nonzero.
- **step-picard-cup-product** [claim](#stmt-prop-cup-product) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-cup-product): Apply canonical nonvanishing to the zero class, compute the family Segre integral, and use exterior algebra to identify the real cup-product ring and spherical vanishing. -> Nonzero quadruple product, degree-two cup-product isomorphism and null-class Segre nonvanishing.
- **step-curves-through-points** [claim](#stmt-thm-family-curves) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-cup-product-2): Kill the ordinary invariant using the opposite coefficient direction, force marked evaluation zeros through spherical nonvanishing, and extract an incident curve limit. -> Positive configurations through every point in the coefficient direction fixed by the positive period projection.
- **step-root-exclusion** [claim](#stmt-prop-root-exclusion) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-root-exclusion): Use the unmarked spherical invariant for a square-minus-two class, extract a positive configuration, and contradict zero taming area under period orthogonality. -> Exclusion of period-orthogonal roots.
- **step-null-lattice-chamber** [claim](#stmt-prop-chamber-class) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-chamber-class): Choose a rational positive vector, use Eichler's normal form to construct a saturated null lattice, bound residual cosets, and avoid their finitely many non-torsion direction circles. -> Primitive integral null class with uniform chamber implication.
- **step-curve-class-alternatives** [claim](#stmt-cor-curve-signs) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-curve-signs): Apply adjunction and anti-invariant period vanishing, then exclude zero projection and nonzero residual roots in both topological cases. -> Aligned intersection signs or a nonzero integral fiber-class multiple.
- **step-fiber-nonsplitting** [claim](#stmt-prop-nonsplitting) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-nonsplitting): Use positive taming area and the class alternatives in a total fiber-class decomposition, then apply intersection positivity and adjunction. -> Reduced irreducible disjoint fiber-class curves through all points, with the stated genus and singularity alternatives.
- **step-sphere-compactness** [claim](#stmt-lem-pencil-compactness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-pencil-compactness): Use a fixed limiting tamer in genus-zero compactness and nonsplitting to eliminate nonconstant bubbles and unstable constant trees. -> Smooth reparametrized convergence, retained mark and openness of immersion.
- **step-exact-first-jet-transversality** [claim](#stmt-lem-pencil-jets) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-pencil-jets): Reduce the universal annihilator to pullback-period constants and a point distribution, eliminate the point term by the elliptic symbol, remove constants with coefficient directions, and apply Sard–Smale. -> Smooth arbitrarily small exact perturbations eliminating critical fiber-class spheres, including relative paths.
- **step-normal-moduli** [claim](#stmt-lem-pencil-normal) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-pencil-normal): Identify normal fields with one-forms, solve the variable-coefficient scalar equation on integral-zero targets, and use the similarity principle for torus kernel sections. -> Smooth normal moduli, unique sphere continuation and torus tube foliations.
- **step-nodal-count-stability** [claim](#stmt-cor-pencil-node-count) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-pencil-node-count): Combine compact sphere moduli with local isolation and continuation to obtain a finite covering over the parameter interval. -> Finite and constant nodal-sphere count.
- **step-fixed-nodal-family** [claim](#stmt-lem-nodal-fixed-family) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-nodal-fixed-family): Embed fibers by section divisors, compare Laurent-coefficient subbundles across the puncture, and identify the reduced cubic closures. -> Holomorphic symplectic isomorphisms of completed families.
- **step-annular-model-periods** [claim](#stmt-lem-nodal-annular-periods) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-nodal-annular-periods): Compute the shear mapping-torus homology and check the fiber and bounding invariant-cycle-sweep periods. -> Equality of annular real cohomology classes.
- **step-collapsing-nodal-model** [claim](#stmt-thm-nodal-model) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-nodal-annular-periods-2): Normalize the periodic monopole potential, complete the Hopf pole, fix Abel periods and the complex family, compare Fourier tails on annuli, and transport polynomial intrinsic charts. -> Fixed nodal elliptic neighborhood with exact local equal-square forms, exponential annular comparison and polynomial intrinsic geometry.
- **step-exact-nodal-insertion** [claim](#stmt-lem-pencil-insertion) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-pencil-insertion): Match tangent and volume data, use a radial exact primitive at the crossing, and use logarithmic transverse cutoffs along the remaining normalization. -> Exact positive pair path retaining the sphere and inserting a full smaller holomorphic model neighborhood.
- **step-global-torus-pencil** [claim](#stmt-thm-pencil) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-pencil-insertion-2): Make spheres immersed, insert and retain all nodes, use relative path transversality and node-count stability, then assemble saturated torus tubes and model disks into a Hausdorff smooth quotient. -> Smooth proper torus fibration with ordinary nodal singular fibers and exact positive pair path.
- **step-fiber-averaging** [claim](#stmt-lem-regular-averaging) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-regular-averaging): Patch Haar averaging through integral angle transitions and solve the zero-average complex by vertical Hodge homotopy followed by horizontal-degree induction. -> Differentiation-commuting average and zero-average primitives preserving base support.
- **step-mixed-pair-convexity** [claim](#stmt-lem-regular-mixed-cone) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-regular-mixed-cone): Express mixed forms by a matrix, identify the two Lorentz cones of its traceless part, and check that basic additions wedge trivially. -> Convex definite-pair components and wedge-matrix preservation under basic additions.
- **step-smooth-tamer-selection** [claim](#stmt-lem-smooth-tamers) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-smooth-tamers): Choose fixed representatives on parameter neighborhoods and patch them with a nonnegative parameter partition of unity using prescribed endpoint weights. -> Smooth fixed-class tamer family with the required endpoints.
- **step-preparation-taming-class** [claim](#stmt-lem-regular-tamer-path) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-regular-tamer-path): Add a sufficiently large positive basic form to obtain a known tamer, use curve-sign alternatives to prove positivity of the original third class, and apply the taming-cone criterion. -> Availability of the original third taming class and smooth representative selection.
- **step-regular-prepared-data** [claim](#stmt-prop-regular-preparation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-regular-tamer-path-2): Average the pair, construct and locally normalize a unit-fiber-area form, remove its total pairings, and make exact basic pair changes to impose pointwise orthogonality. -> Invariant pair and orthogonal closed unit-fiber-area form, retaining nodal models and original triple classes.
- **step-approximate-collapsing-geometry** [claim](#stmt-lem-auxiliary-geometry) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-auxiliary-geometry): Glue the invariant equal-square form to exact local models using matching annular periods, normalize cohomological moments, and estimate core, regular and annular geometry. -> Polynomial finite-order geometry and Sobolev constants with exponentially small normalized residual.
- **step-exact-linear-inverse** [claim](#stmt-lem-auxiliary-inverse) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-auxiliary-inverse): Recover self-dual data from the Gram matrix, verify harmonic moments, construct an exact form using the Green operator, and estimate it by the exact-form Stokes identity and Weitzenböck induction. -> Unique exact-form inverse with polynomial Sobolev norm bounds and no required one-form spectral gap.
- **step-auxiliary-exact-volume** [claim](#stmt-thm-auxiliary-solution) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-auxiliary-inverse-2): Run the nonlinear wedge correction as a contraction on exact Sobolev forms, retain mean-zero moments by Stokes, and bootstrap a Coulomb primitive through the elliptic linearization. -> Smooth closed equal-square orthogonal auxiliary form with positive fiber sign.
- **step-auxiliary-uniform-chamber** [claim](#stmt-prop-auxiliary-class) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-auxiliary-inverse-3): Compute the auxiliary class modulo the fiber class by restriction, determine its dominant coefficient from the square, and complete the Lorentzian negative-direction square to exclude all negative integral fiber pairings at once. -> Bounded transverse class, dominant positive fiber coefficient and uniform transfer of curve positivity to the original third class.
- **step-kahler-class-volume** [claim](#stmt-lem-endpoint-kahler-class) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-endpoint-kahler-class): Apply the compact-surface Kähler criterion, numerical cone positivity and the prescribed-volume theorem. -> Kähler class and a cohomologous representative with the prescribed square.
- **step-hodge-type-characterization** [claim](#stmt-lem-endpoint-hodge-type) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-endpoint-hodge-type): Use the nowhere-zero holomorphic volume form to identify the holomorphic cohomology line and its positive real period plane, then apply Hodge orthogonality. -> Real Hodge type characterized by period orthogonality.
- **step-main-fixed-class-endpoint** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-endpoint-hodge-type-2): Prepare the pair, choose the uniform auxiliary class, perform successive Kähler volume steps in the original remaining classes, keep the third class available by the curve criterion, and concatenate smooth positive paths. -> Smooth fixed-class path to a parallel self-dual hyperkähler triple in the original ordered classes.
- **step-individual-kahler-realization** [claim](#stmt-cor-individual-kahler) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-individual-kahler): Normalize the endpoint linear combination and apply Moser isotopy to its fixed-class symplectic path, pulling back the endpoint metric and complex structure. -> Individual hyperkähler Kähler realization of the original linear-combination form.
- **step-smooth-type-classification** [claim](#stmt-cor-smooth-type) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-smooth-type): Use the global hyperkähler endpoint and compact hyperkähler surface classification, then identify the standard smooth types. -> Standard K3 or torus diffeomorphism type.

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-fixed-class-deformation**: The normalized positive closed triple admits a smooth deformation through positive closed triples that preserves every constituent cohomology class and ends in parallel self-dual forms for a hyperkähler metric.
- **invariant-individual-kahler-realisation**: Every fixed nonzero coefficient combination of the initial triple is itself a Kähler form for a separately chosen hyperkähler metric and parallel integrable complex structure.
- **invariant-taming-implies-compatible-existence**: A symplectically tamed smooth almost-complex structure admits a smooth compatible symplectic form; this assertion does not prescribe the compatible form’s cohomology class.
- **invariant-prescribed-taming-class**: A positive-square class in the same positive component as a known positive-square taming class contains a smooth tamer when it pairs positively with every irreducible closed pseudoholomorphic curve and the closed definite-pair hypotheses hold.
- **invariant-auxiliary-class-separation**: The auxiliary equal-square form completes the prepared pair to a positive triple, but its class is auxiliary. Its uniform chamber comparison supplies positivity in the original third class for later pair deformations.
- **invariant-exact-form-inverse**: The linearized wedge equations have a unique exact two-form solution for top-form data with vanishing integrals. The inverse has polynomial Sobolev bounds without requiring a positive spectral gap on one-forms.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-use-outside-closed-smooth-regime**: Apply the deformation conclusion to a noncompact manifold, a manifold with boundary, or forms lacking the required smoothness. -> The source does not establish the deformation conclusion outside its closed smooth setting; the proof uses global compactness, cohomology and integration arguments.
- **anti-use-degenerate-positive-triple**: Treat a rank-deficient or indefinite triple as admissible input. -> The associated positive conformal geometry and definite-pair constructions require strict pointwise positivity and independence.
- **anti-use-flow-convergence**: Use existence of the deformation path as a convergence or uniqueness certificate for the hypersymplectic flow. -> The deformation existence statement is explicitly separated from convergence and uniqueness of that flow.
- **anti-use-simultaneous-moser-transport**: Choose one transport that simultaneously makes every initial constituent a Kähler form for the same transported hyperkähler structure. -> The individual realization chooses the compatible structure separately for each coefficient combination.
- **anti-use-unrestricted-prescribed-class**: Infer that the compatible symplectic form supplied by taming has the original taming class. -> Compatible-form existence has an unrestricted class; prescribed-class taming requires the additional definite-pair and intersection hypotheses.
- **anti-use-unchecked-linear-moments**: Apply the exact-form inverse to arbitrary top-form data or permit a correction that changes the auxiliary class. -> Exactness imposes vanishing integrals in every wedge slot, and the inverse is asserted for exact two-form corrections.
- **anti-use-auxiliary-form-as-original-endpoint**: Substitute the auxiliary equal-square form directly for the original third form in the claimed fixed-class endpoint. -> The auxiliary form uses a different cohomology class; the chamber comparison and subsequent Kähler steps recover the original classes.
- **anti-use-finite-numerical-certification**: Certify the global deformation theorem through agreement on finitely many sampled forms or numerical meshes. -> Finite sampling does not establish smooth global existence, preservation of cohomology, or strict positivity at every point throughout the path.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The principal result constructs a smooth deformation of differential forms on a closed manifold, using current separation, compactness limits, elliptic inverses and Kähler existence theorems. It does not specify a finite input representation, an effective stopping rule or certified discretisation errors. The source states: “We finish by proving spatial smoothness; no simultaneous estimate over infinitely many derivative orders is needed.” This analytic existence construction is not a finite constructive result that can be certified by an executable reference and finite test vectors.

| software | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The smooth deformation theorem supplies no finite representation of its input forms, executable deformation procedure, or stopping criterion for a software implementation. |

| crypto_security | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The integral intersection lattice constrains geometric curve classes; its root-exclusion property supplies no cryptographic construction or computational hardness assertion. |
| machine_learning | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The compatible-family construction concerns closed forms over a coefficient sphere. It introduces no learned model, training objective, or statistical generalisation guarantee. |
| optimisation_operations_research | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The taming-class criterion requires positivity against every irreducible closed pseudoholomorphic curve. The paper does not turn this condition into a finite constraint set or an optimisation algorithm. |

<a id="pm-s6"></a>
## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-closed-smooth-geometric-input** (hypothesis): The deformation theorem requires a closed connected oriented smooth four-manifold and a smooth hypersymplectic input. Boundary, noncompact and lower-regularity variants are outside the stated result. Blocked use: ['Apply the deformation conclusion to manifolds with boundary or noncompact manifolds.', 'Replace smooth input by weak differential forms without a separate regularity theorem.']
- **limit-strict-pointwise-positivity** (hypothesis): The input forms must be closed and span a pointwise positive definite plane of the stated dimension. Degenerate or indefinite triples do not satisfy this definition. Blocked use: ['Invoke the theorem when positivity holds only at sampled points.', 'Allow the wedge-product matrix to become degenerate during the deformation.']
- **limit-normalized-versus-original-basis** (formal_scope): The displayed normalized endpoint identity applies after intersection normalization. For an arbitrary original basis, the endpoint retains its original Gram matrix. Blocked use: ['Assert the normalized pointwise endpoint identity for an unnormalized original ordered basis.', 'Treat normalization as preserving each original constituent class without undoing the coefficient change.']
- **limit-existence-not-flow-convergence** (formal_scope): Existence of the constructed deformation does not establish convergence or uniqueness of the hypersymplectic flow. Blocked use: ['Use the main theorem as a global flow convergence certificate.', 'Identify the constructed path with a unique flow trajectory.']
- **limit-individual-realizations-not-simultaneous** (formal_scope): Individual Kähler realizations choose their compatible structures separately for each fixed coefficient combination. Blocked use: ['Infer a common transport simultaneously realizing the original triple under one chosen hyperkähler structure.']
- **limit-compatible-class-unrestricted** (formal_scope): Compatible-form existence does not prescribe the compatible class. Prescribed-class taming uses a separate criterion with additional geometric hypotheses. Blocked use: ['Infer that a compatible form has the same cohomology class as the given tamer.', 'Apply the prescribed-class criterion to an arbitrary tamed structure without a closed definite anti-invariant pair.']
- **limit-full-taming-cone-conditions** (hypothesis): The prescribed-class criterion requires the stated positive intersection index, a closed definite anti-invariant pair, a known positive-square taming class, the same positive component, and strict positivity against every irreducible closed curve. Blocked use: ['Certify a taming class from positive square alone.', 'Replace the universal curve condition by checking selected curve classes.', 'Drop the positive-component condition.']
- **limit-density-weight-restrictions** (hypothesis): Smooth density-weight closedness is proved for the specified separator constructions and bounded smooth weights vanishing at zero. Threshold closedness follows through the separate bounded-weight limit. Blocked use: ['Assert closedness for arbitrary measurable weights of a positive current.', 'Reverse the smoothing and threshold limits without justifying uniform derivative control.']
- **limit-integral-cycle-regularity-order** (hypothesis): Representing the threshold cycles by irreducible curves requires taming; the proof establishes compatible-form existence before invoking integral-cycle regularity. Blocked use: ['Invoke the curve representation for an untamed almost-complex structure.', "Skip the compatibility step needed for the regularity theorem's local hypothesis."]
- **limit-varying-background-compactness** (hypothesis): The incidence compactness result assumes smoothly converging compatible backgrounds, a fixed Spin-c structure, solutions of the specified equations, and a parameter tending to infinity. Blocked use: ['Extract the asserted curve limit from backgrounds with only uncontrolled weak convergence.', 'Retain marked zeros while changing the spinor eigenline class or equation normalization.']
- **limit-configurations-before-nonsplitting** (formal_scope): The marked families theorem initially produces positive configurations. Reduction to a single irreducible component depends on the specially chosen chamber class and the later nonsplitting argument. Blocked use: ['Infer irreducibility for every nonzero integral null class from point-incidence existence alone.']
- **limit-rational-defect-before-immersion** (edge_case): A rational fiber-class curve of total adjunction defect one need not initially be immersed. The ordinary transverse node conclusion requires immersion. Blocked use: ['Treat every initial rational fiber-class image as an ordinary nodal fiber.', 'Omit exact first-jet perturbations before inserting holomorphic nodal neighborhoods.']
- **limit-node-count-immersed-path** (hypothesis): Constancy of the sphere count requires a compact smooth fixed-period path on which all fiber-class spheres remain immersed. Blocked use: ['Assert node-count constancy through a path containing critical sphere parametrizations.', 'Use endpoint immersion alone to establish count constancy throughout an unperturbed path.']
- **limit-annular-periods-before-gluing** (hypothesis): Exact annular gluing requires equality of both the fiber period and the invariant-cycle sweep period. A small pointwise discrepancy does not by itself establish exactness. Blocked use: ['Construct an exact annular primitive from norm smallness alone.', 'Match fiber areas while ignoring the invariant-cycle sweep.']
- **limit-fixed-annuli-versus-varying-core-charts** (approximation): Annular comparison uses fixed smooth charts, whereas the intrinsic core charts may vary with the collapsing parameter. Estimates are stated at each fixed finite derivative order. Blocked use: ['Infer uniformly controlled transport derivatives in a separately fixed atlas near the nodal core.', 'Claim simultaneous control over every derivative order from a fixed-order estimate.', 'Move the annuli with the collapsing parameter without establishing a new comparison estimate.']
- **limit-exact-correction-moments** (hypothesis): The exact-form inverse requires vanishing integrals in all input wedge slots. Uniqueness concerns the exact correction form, rather than its primitive. Blocked use: ['Solve arbitrary top-form residuals using the asserted inverse before normalizing their moments.', 'Claim uniqueness of a one-form primitive without fixing its additional freedom.', 'Permit nonlinear corrections that change the auxiliary cohomology class.']
- **limit-infinite-dimensional-contraction** (nonconstructive): The nonlinear correction uses contraction in an infinite-dimensional space of exact Sobolev forms after fixing a finite differentiation order and choosing a sufficiently small parameter. This does not supply a finite discretization or a general executable stopping contract. Blocked use: ['Treat a discretized fixed-point iteration as a certificate of the smooth auxiliary solution without an approximation theorem.', 'Declare a universal numerical parameter threshold from unspecified geometry-dependent constants.']
- **limit-auxiliary-class-not-original-third-class** (formal_scope): The equal-square auxiliary form has an auxiliary class. Recovering the original third class requires the uniform chamber comparison and the subsequent Kähler endpoint construction. Blocked use: ['Substitute the auxiliary form directly for the original third constituent while claiming preservation of its class.', 'Choose a separate small parameter for each later curve instead of establishing the uniform chamber estimate.']
- **limit-damaged-uniform-transfer-statement** (unknown): The supplied uniform-transfer display has a bare curve-class positivity antecedent without naming the pairing. The proof explicitly assumes positive pairing with the auxiliary class. That proof condition must not be silently inserted into an exact quotation of the statement. Blocked use: ['Treat the damaged display as a self-contained numerical criterion.', 'Interpret curve-class positivity as an independently defined order on cohomology.']
- **limit-kahler-volume-hypotheses** (hypothesis): The endpoint volume criterion requires a compact connected complex surface with even first Betti number, a positive-square real class of the stated Hodge type containing a closed tamer, and a positive volume form with matching total integral. Blocked use: ['Apply the Kähler endpoint step before proving integrability and the required Hodge type.', 'Prescribe a volume form whose total integral differs from the class square.']
- **limit-no-finite-global-certificate** (formal_scope): The paper's smooth existence and classification conclusions are not finite algorithmic certificates for arbitrary encoded manifolds or differential forms. A finite computational model and general complexity contract are ABSENT. Blocked use: ['Claim that finite samples prove positivity and class preservation over the entire smooth deformation.', 'Interpret the smooth-type conclusion as an unconditional manifold recognition algorithm.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


Every smooth normalized positive triple of closed two-forms on a closed connected oriented four-manifold admits a smooth deformation, with each cohomology class fixed, to a hyperkähler triple. This resolves Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction

A *hypersymplectic structure* on an oriented four-manifold is a triple of closed real two-forms whose pointwise span is three-dimensional and positive definite for the wedge product. Such a triple determines a conformal structure, but its forms need not be parallel. After a constant normalization of their intersection matrix, the question is whether one can deform the forms to a hyperkähler triple while retaining their three cohomology classes.

<a id="stmt-thm-main"></a>
<div id="thm:main" class="theorem">

<a id="eq:intro-endpoint"></a>
**Theorem 1**. *Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth four-manifold, and let $\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3)$ be a smooth hypersymplectic structure normalized by <a id="eq:intro-normalization"></a>$$\label{eq:intro-normalization}
 \int_X\omega_i\wedge\omega_j=\delta_{ij}.$$ There is a smooth family of hypersymplectic structures $\omega(t)$, $0\le t\le1$, such that $$\omega(0)=\omega,\qquad [\omega_i(t)]=[\omega_i]
 \quad (i=1,2,3),$$ and a positive volume form $\mu_1$ with $$\label{eq:intro-endpoint}
 \omega_i(1)\wedge\omega_j(1)=2\delta_{ij}\mu_1.$$ The endpoint forms are parallel and self-dual for a hyperkähler metric.*

</div>

For an arbitrary positive volume form $\mu$, write $\omega_i\wedge\omega_j=2\mathcal Q_{ij}\mu$. There is a unique choice of $\mu$ for which $\det\mathcal Q=1$, and <a href="#eq:intro-endpoint" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:intro-endpoint">[eq:intro-endpoint]</a> is exactly $\mathcal Q=I_3$ in this convention. The statement is unaffected by a constant orthogonal change of the ordered triple.

The normalization also specifies the conclusion for any initial positive closed triple. Let $G_{ij}=\int_X\omega_i\wedge\omega_j$; this matrix is positive definite. Choose a constant invertible real matrix $L$ with $LGL^{\mathsf T}=I_3$ and apply [thm:main](#thm:main) to $L\omega$. Applying $L^{-1}$ to the resulting path preserves positivity and each original class. Its endpoint satisfies $$\omega_i(1)\wedge\omega_j(1)=2G_{ij}\mu_1,$$ where $\mu_1$ is the volume form of the normalized endpoint metric. Thus the original basis consists of parallel self-dual forms for a hyperkähler metric, with its original Gram matrix $G$.

<a id="stmt-cor-individual-kahler"></a>
<div id="cor:individual-kahler" class="corollary">

**Corollary 2** (Individual Kähler realizations). *Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth four-manifold with a smooth positive triple $\omega$ of closed real two-forms. For every fixed $c\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, the form $\alpha_c=\sum_i c_i\omega_i$ is a Kähler form for a parallel integrable complex structure $J_c$ of some hyperkähler metric $g_c$ on $X$: $$\alpha_c(v,w)=g_c(J_cv,w).$$ The compatible structure is chosen separately for each $c$; no simultaneous transport of the triple is asserted.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-cor-individual-kahler"><summary>Proof of stmt-cor-individual-kahler</summary>

*Proof.* Use the fixed-class path for the original basis described above and put $\alpha_t=\sum_i c_i\omega_i(t)$. Positivity of the pointwise wedge-product matrix gives $\alpha_t\wedge\alpha_t>0$. Thus $\alpha_t$ is symplectic, and its class is fixed because each $[\omega_i(t)]$ is fixed.

For the endpoint metric $g$, set $r_c=(c^{\mathsf T}Gc)^{1/2}>0$. The endpoint identities show that $\alpha_1/r_c$ is parallel and self-dual with $g$-norm $\sqrt2$. It therefore defines a parallel integrable complex structure $J^{\mathrm{end}}_c$ with $\alpha_1/r_c=g(J^{\mathrm{end}}_c\,\cdot,\cdot)$. Hence $\alpha_1$ is its Kähler form for the hyperkähler metric $r_cg$.

Since $X$ is closed, Moser’s theorem gives an isotopy $\phi_{c,t}$ with $\phi_{c,0}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\phi_{c,t}^*\alpha_t=\alpha_c$. Pulling back $r_cg$ and $J^{\mathrm{end}}_c$ by $\phi_{c,1}$ gives the claimed hyperkähler metric and compatible integrable structure on $X$. Fine and Yao note this Moser implication for a constituent in (Fine and Yao 2018, sec. 1) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[FineYao2017](#ref-FineYao2017)]. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-cor-smooth-type"></a>
<div id="cor:smooth-type" class="corollary">

**Corollary 3** (Smooth type). *Let $X$ be a closed connected smooth four-manifold admitting a smooth positive triple of closed real two-forms. Then $X$ is diffeomorphic to the standard K3 manifold or to $T^4$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-cor-smooth-type"><summary>Proof of stmt-cor-smooth-type</summary>

*Proof.* Give $X$ the orientation induced by the triple. The normalization above and [thm:main](#thm:main) give a global hyperkähler triple on $X$. Choosing one of its complex structures makes $X$ a compact Kähler surface with a nowhere-vanishing holomorphic two-form. The compact hyperkähler surface classification (Boyer 1988, sec. 2, p. 162) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[Boyer1988](#ref-Boyer1988)] therefore identifies $X$ itself as a complex two-torus or a K3 surface. A complex two-torus is smoothly $T^4$, while every complex K3 surface is diffeomorphic to a nonsingular quartic surface in $\mathbf P^3$, the standard K3 manifold (Kodaira 1970, 58) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[Kodaira1970](#ref-Kodaira1970)]. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### History and significance

Donaldson’s study of closed two-forms on four-manifolds links their pointwise wedge-product geometry to nonlinear elliptic equations (Donaldson 2006) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Donaldson2006](#ref-Donaldson2006)]. His Question 3 in Section 5.3 asks whether a compact oriented four-manifold carrying a positive closed triple admits a hyperkähler structure. In the same section he proposes a prescribed-volume continuity argument in the simply connected case, conditional on a priori estimates and an auxiliary involution. The involution keeps the evolving form in a fixed cohomology class (Donaldson 2006, sec. 5.3) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[Donaldson2006](#ref-Donaldson2006)]. Fine and Yao formulate the normalized deformation problem, retaining all three cohomology classes, as Conjecture 1.1 of (Fine and Yao 2018) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[FineYao2017](#ref-FineYao2017)]. resolves this deformation conjecture positively. Keeping the classes connects the given triple to a metric with its prescribed periods, beyond existence of some hyperkähler metric on the same manifold.

The main analytic approach has been the hypersymplectic flow. Fine and Yao obtained this flow by reducing the $G_2$-Laplacian flow on the product with a three-torus. They proved that a finite-time solution extends while the associated seven-dimensional scalar curvature, equivalently the torsion, remains bounded (Fine and Yao 2018, Theorem 1.3) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[FineYao2017](#ref-FineYao2017)]. Their later work gives an integral torsion extension criterion, global existence near pointwise orthogonality, and subsequential convergence of global solutions under additional geometric bounds (Fine and Yao 2019, Theorems 4.7, 4.10, 4.15 and 4.16) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[FineYao2020](#ref-FineYao2020)].

Several restricted classes admit complete convergence results. Huang, Wang and Yao proved convergence, after pullback by diffeomorphisms, for simple-type hypersymplectic structures on the standard four-torus, a diagonal one-variable class (Huang, Wang, and Yao 2018, Theorems 3.5 and 3.6) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[HuangWangYao2018](#ref-HuangWangYao2018)]. Picard and Suan treated $G_2$ flows associated with Kähler Calabi–Yau data; their complex-dimension-two case supplies a hypersymplectic convergence theorem (Picard and Suan 2024, Theorem 1.3) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[PicardSuan2024](#ref-PicardSuan2024)]. Fine, He and Yao extended the simple-type convergence result, modulo diffeomorphisms, to $T^3$-invariant triples on $T^4$ in symmetric normal form (Fine, He, and Yao 2025a, Theorem 1.5) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[FineHeYao2024](#ref-FineHeYao2024)]. They subsequently proved a linear cohomologous isotopy to a hyperkähler triple when an effective smooth circle action preserves the initial triple (Fine, He, and Yao 2025b, Theorem 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[FineHeYao2025](#ref-FineHeYao2025)]. Related reductions and coflow constructions appear in work of Petcu, Yao and Zhou, and Karigiannis, Picard and Suan (Petcu 2026; Yao and Zhou 2026; Karigiannis, Picard, and Suan 2026) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[Petcu2026](#ref-Petcu2026), [YaoZhou2026](#ref-YaoZhou2026), [KarigiannisPicardSuan2026](#ref-KarigiannisPicardSuan2026)]. These results retain their stated symmetry or integrability hypotheses. The path constructed here starts from an arbitrary positive closed triple; its existence is a separate question from convergence or uniqueness for the hypersymplectic flow.

The topology already places strong restrictions on such a triple. Any two of its forms determine an almost-complex structure whose canonical line is trivial, and the third form tames that structure. Here a real two-form $\beta$ *tames* $J$ if $\beta(v,Jv)>0$ for every nonzero vector $v$; it is *compatible* if it is also $J$-invariant. A closed tamer is symplectic. Bauer’s bound for symplectic four-manifolds with torsion first Chern class (Bauer 2008, Corollary 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[Bauer2008](#ref-Bauer2008)], together with the three positive period classes, gives $b^+=3$, where $b^+$ is the positive index of the intersection form. The resulting free intersection lattice is the K3 lattice or three hyperbolic planes. These facts supply the lattice used below; they do not presuppose a smooth identification of the initial manifold with a K3 surface or torus.

For controlling closed positive forms, Sullivan’s structure currents provide the cone-duality framework (Sullivan 1976) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[Sullivan1976](#ref-Sullivan1976)]. Harvey and Lawson developed the positive-current characterization of Kähler geometry (Harvey and Lawson 1983) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[HarveyLawson1983](#ref-HarveyLawson1983)]. A separate article proves that every tamed smooth almost-complex structure on a closed connected real four-manifold admits a compatible symplectic form (OpenAI 2026, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[OpenAITaming2026](#ref-OpenAITaming2026)]. Its current estimates and density-splitting argument are also used here, with the needed proofs included in [sec:current-energy](#sec:current-energy), [sec:density-splitting](#sec:density-splitting). In particular, smooth density-weight closedness already appears in the proof in Section 6 of that article. Its compatible class is unrestricted. The prescribed taming class is obtained instead from [thm:taming-cone](#thm:taming-cone), under its closed definite-pair and $b^+=3$ hypotheses. Its proof uses the class separator and converts closed normalized density thresholds into curves, using Preiss’s rectifiability theorem and Rivière–Tian’s regularity theorem for integral cycles (Preiss 1987; Rivière and Tian 2009) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[Preiss1987](#ref-Preiss1987), [RiviereTian2009](#ref-RiviereTian2009)]. This supplies the prescribed taming class needed along the deformation, independently of a general comparison between the tame and compatible cones.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### The main ideas

The proof organizes the deformation around a pair of forms. Write an ordered triple as $(A,C,B)$, and write products of forms for wedge products. The positive plane spanned by $A,C$ determines an almost-complex structure $J$, with sign chosen so that $B$ tames it. A pair deformation gives the desired triple deformation provided the original third class continues to contain a tamer. The argument first proves a criterion for this availability, then constructs a fibration and an auxiliary equal-square pair, and finally uses two classical Kähler steps to reach the endpoint.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
###### Currents and a prescribed class.

Separation of the cone of positive forms gives a positive current obstructing a desired closed form. Quadratic mass estimates bound its mass in a ball of radius $r$ by $Kr^2$ for a fixed constant $K$. Resolvent regularization also controls how its complex-line directions vary on that scale. Together these estimates prove closedness after weighting by smooth functions of the two-dimensional density. The zero-density part can then be handled by the intersection form, while normalized thresholds of the positive-density part give integral pseudoholomorphic cycles. Compatibility is proved before the integral-cycle regularity theorem is applied, so that its local symplectic hypothesis is available.

The output is [thm:tamed-compatible](#thm:tamed-compatible), [thm:taming-cone](#thm:taming-cone). For the second theorem, let $V$ be the intersection-orthogonal complement of $[A],[C]$. It has Lorentz signature because $b^+=3$. A positive-square class $H\in V$ is a taming class if it is in the same positive component as a known positive-square taming class $U\in V$ and pairs positively with every irreducible closed $J$-curve. The criterion will keep $[B]$ available as the pair changes.

<a id="pm-h-6"></a>
###### Marked curves and a torus fibration.

The initial triple supplies an entire coefficient sphere of almost-complex structures: for $v\in S^2$, the forms $a\cdot\omega$ with $a\cdot v=0$ constitute its anti-invariant plane (a form $\xi$ is anti-invariant when $\xi(Ju,Jw)=-\xi(u,w)$), and $v\cdot\omega$ tames the corresponding structure. Compatible forms can be selected smoothly over this sphere by a constant-rank elliptic correction. After projecting their classes to the original positive period plane and normalizing, one obtains a degree-one map to its unit sphere. Li proposed using such winding sphere families, parametrized wall crossing, and Taubes’s curve correspondence to construct elliptic fibrations (Li 2010, sec. 7.4.1) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[Li2010SCY](#ref-Li2010SCY)]. The marked-family construction below carries out this approach for the coefficient sphere of the initial triple. Li–Liu’s families wall-crossing and index formulas (Li and Liu 2001) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[LiLiu2001](#ref-LiLiu2001)], together with Taubes’s canonical nonvanishing and large-parameter curve extraction (Taubes 1994, 1996, 1999) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[Taubes1994](#ref-Taubes1994), [Taubes1996](#ref-Taubes1996), [Taubes1999](#ref-Taubes1999)], then give curves through every point in a chosen nonzero integral square-zero class. To impose passage through a chosen point, the proof requires one component of the Seiberg–Witten spinor to vanish there. As the parameter moves over the sphere, the line containing that component also varies and has degree of absolute value one. Its contribution must be retained in the marked wall-crossing calculation, even though the underlying Spin-c structure is fixed throughout the family.

The integral class is chosen to prevent any such curve configuration from splitting. Eichler’s criterion supplies the lattice normal form (Gritsenko, Hulek, and Sankaran 2009, Proposition 3.3(i)) <a id="pm-cite-22"></a>[[GritsenkoHulekSankaran2009](#ref-GritsenkoHulekSankaran2009)]; a further finite-coset argument works for the arbitrary real positive period plane of the original triple. Pseudoholomorphic adjunction and positivity of intersections then reduce the possible fibers to tori and rational curves with one singularity (McDuff and Salamon 2012; Wendl 2020) <a id="pm-cite-23"></a>[[McDuffSalamon2012](#ref-McDuffSalamon2012), [Wendl2020](#ref-Wendl2020)]. To obtain ordinary nodes, we prove transversality using exact perturbations of $A,C$ with $B$ fixed. The first-jet method is related to that of Oh and Zhu (Oh and Zhu 2009) <a id="pm-cite-24"></a>[[OhZhu2008](#ref-OhZhu2008)], but the allowable closed-form variations require their own cokernel calculation. Relative nodal replacement and local deformation theory now produce the fibration of [thm:pencil](#thm:pencil): a proper map from $X$ to a closed oriented surface, with torus regular fibers and rational singular fibers having one ordinary node.

<a id="pm-h-7"></a>
###### An auxiliary volume equation.

The fibration supplies classes with small positive fiber area. Near a nodal fiber we use the Gibbons–Hawking construction (Gibbons and Hawking 1978) <a id="pm-cite-25"></a>[[GibbonsHawking1978](#ref-GibbonsHawking1978)] and the periodic Ooguri–Vafa model (Ooguri and Vafa 1996) <a id="pm-cite-26"></a>[[OoguriVafa1996](#ref-OoguriVafa1996)]. Gross and Wilson developed the corresponding mathematical collapsing and semi-flat gluing methods for elliptic K3 surfaces (Gross and Wilson 2000) <a id="pm-cite-27"></a>[[GrossWilson2000](#ref-GrossWilson2000)]. Here the nodal holomorphic model is constructed independently, since a global complex structure is not yet available. On fixed annuli the model and regular data agree up to exponentially small error. Matching the fiber area and the period on the surface swept out by the monodromy-invariant fiber cycle ensures that the discrepancy has a primitive.

After exact preparation of the pair, these local forms glue to an approximate auxiliary form of fiber area $\epsilon$. The correction in [thm:auxiliary-solution](#thm:auxiliary-solution) is solved on exact two-forms. For any Riemannian metric on the oriented closed four-manifold, let $h^+$ denote the self-dual part of an exact two-form $h$. The exact-form identity used in Donaldson’s elliptic formulation (Donaldson 2006, sec. 2, proof of Proposition 1; Section 4, Lemma 1) <a id="pm-cite-28"></a>[[Donaldson2006](#ref-Donaldson2006)] $$\|h\|_{L^2}^2=2\|h^+\|_{L^2}^2\qquad(h\text{ exact})$$ controls the inverse while the fibers collapse. The remaining finite Sobolev estimates lose only powers of $\epsilon^{-1}$, which are absorbed by the exponentially small gluing error. This produces a closed form $D$ satisfying $AD=CD=0$ and $D^2=A^2$. The class inequality in [prop:auxiliary-class](#prop:auxiliary-class) holds for all later curves at one fixed choice of $\epsilon$; it transfers positivity from $[D]$ to the original class $[B]$.

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
###### Two Kähler steps in the original classes.

The closed equal-square pair $A,D$ defines an integrable complex structure with holomorphic two-form $A\pm iD$, choosing the sign so that $C$ tames it. The compact-surface criteria of Buchdahl and Lamari, and the numerical Kähler-cone criterion, put $[C]$ in the Kähler cone (Buchdahl 1999; Lamari 1999; Demailly and Păun 2004) <a id="pm-cite-29"></a>[[Buchdahl1999](#ref-Buchdahl1999), [Lamari1999](#ref-Lamari1999), [DemaillyPaun2004](#ref-DemaillyPaun2004)]. Yau’s volume theorem (Yau 1978) <a id="pm-cite-30"></a>[[Yau1978](#ref-Yau1978)] gives $C_1\in[C]$ with $C_1^2=A^2$. Interpolate from $C$ to $C_1$; the uniform class inequality and the taming criterion keep $[B]$ available throughout. The pair $A,C_1$ is now itself an integrable equal-square pair. A second Kähler step in $[B]$ gives $B_1$, completing the hyperkähler triple. Smooth selection of the third forms, with both endpoints prescribed, gives the actual path $(A,C_t,B_t)$ shown in [fig:endpoint-path](#fig:endpoint-path). Every component retains its original class.

<a id="pm-h-9"></a>
#### Organization and conventions

establishes the preliminary geometry and topology. The positive-current results occupy [sec:current-energy](#sec:current-energy), [sec:density-splitting](#sec:density-splitting). [sec:families](#sec:families), [sec:lattice-chamber](#sec:lattice-chamber), [sec:pencil](#sec:pencil) construct the torus fibration, and [sec:local-models](#sec:local-models), [sec:regular-preparation](#sec:regular-preparation), [sec:auxiliary-volume](#sec:auxiliary-volume) construct the auxiliary equal-square pair. The proof of [thm:main](#thm:main) is completed in [sec:endpoint](#sec:endpoint).

We write products of two-forms for wedge products and products of degree-two cohomology classes for their intersection pairing. Curve classes are identified with their Poincaré duals in cohomology. Integral lattice statements use $$\Lambda=H^2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{torsion}.$$ The original positive period plane is $P=\operatorname{span}\{[\omega_1],[\omega_2],[\omega_3]\}$. No rationality of this plane is assumed. All deformations of forms are smooth in the manifold variable; parameter regularity is stated where it is used. Constants in local estimates may depend on fixed smooth background data and on the indicated finite differentiation order.

<a id="sec:definite-pairs"></a>
### Definite pairs and the coefficient sphere

We first associate an almost-complex structure to a definite pair and identify the condition on a third form that makes the triple positive. This converts the later deformation problem into the choice of taming forms in a prescribed class. We also establish the topological restrictions and the degree-one sphere of structures needed to produce curves in [sec:families](#sec:families).

<a id="stmt-auto-definition-1"></a>
<div class="definition">

**Definition 4**. A pair $(A,C)$ of real two-forms is *definite* if its wedge-product matrix is positive definite at every point. A two-form $B$ *tames* an almost-complex structure $J$ if $B(v,Jv)>0$ for every nonzero tangent vector $v$. It is *compatible* if, in addition, $B(Ju,Jv)=B(u,v)$. When these forms are called symplectic, closedness is included.

</div>

<a id="stmt-lem-definite-pair"></a>
<div id="lem:definite-pair" class="lemma">

**Lemma 5**. *A definite pair $(A,C)$ on an oriented four-manifold determines an almost-complex structure up to sign. Its anti-invariant real two-form bundle is pointwise spanned by $A,C$, and its canonical complex line bundle is trivial. A third form $B$ completes a positive triple if and only if it tames one of the two signs of this almost-complex structure. On a connected manifold the sign is fixed by $B$.*

*A real two-plane is Lagrangian for both $A$ and $C$ if and only if it is a complex line, without specifying its orientation.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-definite-pair"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-definite-pair</summary>

*Proof.* Ratios of positive four-forms are smooth functions. Set <a id="eq:pair-normalization"></a>$$\label{eq:pair-normalization}
 x=\frac{AC}{A^2},\qquad
 y=\left(\frac{C^2}{A^2}-x^2\right)^{1/2}>0,\qquad
 T=\frac{C-xA}{y}.$$ Then $AT=0$ and $T^2=A^2>0$. Consequently $$\Omega=A+iT,\qquad \Omega^2=0,\qquad
 \Omega\overline\Omega=2A^2>0.$$ The form $\Omega$ is complex decomposable and its kernel in the complexified tangent bundle is complementary to its conjugate. Taking this kernel as $T^{0,1}$ defines an almost-complex structure with the given orientation. Replacing $y$ by $-y$ conjugates $\Omega$ and changes $J$ to $-J$. The real and imaginary parts of $\Omega$ span the anti-invariant forms, and $\Omega$ is a nowhere-zero section of the canonical bundle.

Choose any Hermitian metric for $J$. The invariant two-forms are the wedge-orthogonal complement of $\operatorname{span}(A,C)$ and have signature $(1,3)$. For the decomposition $B=B^{1,1}+B^{2,0+0,2}$, the positive-triple condition is exactly $(B^{1,1})^2>0$. A real $(1,1)$ form in complex dimension two has positive square precisely when its two Hermitian eigenvalues have the same strict sign. The positive component is the cone of forms positive on every complex line. The anti-invariant summand vanishes on such lines, so this is equivalent to taming by $B$. The other component is positive for $-J$. Connectedness fixes the choice continuously and globally.

Finally, for independent real vectors $u,v$, $A(u,v)=C(u,v)=0$ is equivalent to $\Omega(u,v)=0$. In a complex two-dimensional vector space with a nondegenerate complex volume form, this says that $u,v$ are complex dependent, equivalently that their real span is a complex line. ◻

</details>

In particular, for fixed $J$ the space of taming two-forms is an open convex cone. Its intersection with the closed representatives of any one class is also convex. The associated notion of positivity will always use the sign of $J$ fixed by a stated tamer.

<a id="stmt-prop-topology"></a>
<div id="prop:topology" class="proposition">

**Proposition 6**. *If $X$ carries a positive closed triple, then $$b^+(X)=3,\qquad
 (b_1(X),b^-(X))=(0,19)\ \text{or}\ (4,3).$$ The free integral intersection lattice is respectively $3H\oplus2(-E_8)$ or $3H$, where $H$ is the hyperbolic plane. Every almost-complex structure obtained from a definite pair in the triple has vanishing integral first Chern class.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prop-topology"><summary>Proof of stmt-prop-topology</summary>

*Proof.* By [lem:definite-pair](#lem:definite-pair), one member of the triple is a symplectic form taming an almost-complex structure whose canonical bundle is trivial. The first Chern class of this symplectic form therefore vanishes: the space of its tamed almost-complex structures is contractible and contains compatible structures. Bauer’s bound for a closed symplectic four-manifold with torsion first Chern class gives $b^+\le3$ (Bauer 2008, Corollary 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-31"></a>[[Bauer2008](#ref-Bauer2008)]. The three independent positive cohomology classes give the reverse inequality.

The characteristic-number identity $c_1^2=2\chi+3\sigma$, obtained from $p_1=c_1^2-2c_2$, the Euler-number identity and the signature theorem (Milnor and Stasheff 1974, Corollaries 11.12 and 15.5, Theorem 19.4) <a id="pm-cite-32"></a>[[MilnorStasheff1974](#ref-MilnorStasheff1974)], together with $b^+=3$, gives $$0=19-4b_1-b^-,\qquad \sigma=4b_1-16.$$ Moreover $w_2\equiv c_1=0\pmod2$, so $X$ is spin (Milnor and Stasheff 1974, Problem 14-B) <a id="pm-cite-33"></a>[[MilnorStasheff1974](#ref-MilnorStasheff1974)]. Rokhlin’s theorem makes $\sigma$ divisible by $16$ (Rokhlin 1952) <a id="pm-cite-34"></a>[[Rokhlin1952](#ref-Rokhlin1952)]. Since $b^-\ge0$, these relations give $b_1\in\{0,4\}$ and the displayed alternatives. Poincaré duality makes the free intersection form unimodular, and the Wu formula makes it even (Milnor and Stasheff 1974, Theorem 11.14) <a id="pm-cite-35"></a>[[MilnorStasheff1974](#ref-MilnorStasheff1974)]. Classification of indefinite even unimodular lattices now gives the two stated forms (Serre 1973, vol. 7, chap. V, Section 2.2, Theorems 5–6) <a id="pm-cite-36"></a>[[Serre1973](#ref-Serre1973)]. Only the intersection lattice has been classified at this stage. ◻

</details>

<a id="eq:pair-harmonic-basis"></a>
The positive three-plane bundle spanned by the triple is the self-dual bundle of a unique oriented conformal structure. Choose one metric $g_0$ in that conformal class. Since the original forms are closed and self-dual, they are harmonic, and $$\label{eq:pair-harmonic-basis}
 \mathcal H^+_{g_0}
 =\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3\}$$ by [prop:topology](#prop:topology). Here the span is the vector space of global forms, with constant coefficients.

For $v\in S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$, let $B_v=v\cdot\omega$ and let $\mathcal A_v$ be the plane of forms $a\cdot\omega$ with $a\perp v$. Choosing the sign tamed by $B_v$ defines an almost-complex structure $J_v$. This construction uses the plane $\mathcal A_v$ itself and does not require a global choice of its ordered basis over $S^2$.

<a id="stmt-lem-twistor-degree"></a>
<div id="lem:twistor-degree" class="lemma">

**Lemma 7**. *The family $J_v$ is smooth and is Hermitian for $g_0$. At every point of $X$ its map to the twistor sphere has degree of absolute value one. The closed $J_v$-anti-invariant forms form the two-dimensional space $\mathcal A_v$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-twistor-degree"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-twistor-degree</summary>

*Proof.* The first assertion follows from the construction and the self-dual description of Hermitian almost-complex structures in dimension four. At a fixed point, let $K$ be the positive Gram matrix of the triple for $g_0$. A vector normal to the coefficient plane $v^\perp$, for this Gram matrix, has coefficients $K^{-1}v$. Its pairing with $B_v$ is positive. Thus, after normalization, the fundamental forms give the map $$v\longmapsto\frac{K^{-1}v}{|K^{-1}v|}$$ in radial coefficient coordinates. Positive definite matrices connect to the identity through positive definite matrices, so this map has degree one. The orientation convention identifying coefficient and twistor spheres can change only its sign.

A closed anti-invariant form is self-dual for $g_0$, hence harmonic. By <a href="#eq:pair-harmonic-basis" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:pair-harmonic-basis">[eq:pair-harmonic-basis]</a> it is a constant combination of the original triple. It is anti-invariant for $J_v$ exactly when that coefficient vector lies in $v^\perp$. This proves the final assertion. ◻

</details>

<a id="eq:pair-lorentz-space"></a>
After a constant orthogonal change of coefficients we will denote a chosen original ordered triple by $(A,C,B)$. For all later exact deformations of the pair, set $$\label{eq:pair-lorentz-space}
 V=[A]^\perp\cap[C]^\perp\subset H^2(X;\mathbb R).$$ This space has signature $(1,b^-)$, and $[B]\in V$ is a unit timelike vector. It determines the future component of the timelike cone.

<a id="stmt-lem-complex-symplectic"></a>
<div id="lem:complex-symplectic" class="lemma">

**Lemma 8**. *Let $A,D$ be closed real two-forms with $AD=0$ and $A^2=D^2>0$ pointwise. Then $A+iD$ defines an integrable complex structure, and is a nowhere-zero holomorphic two-form for it. If a closed third form $C$ has $AC=DC=0$ and $C^2=A^2$, then the resulting triple is hyperkähler, after choosing the sign of the complex structure so that $C$ is positive.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-complex-symplectic"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-complex-symplectic</summary>

*Proof.* Set $\Omega=A+iD$ and use its kernel as $T^{0,1}$ as in [lem:definite-pair](#lem:definite-pair). For vector fields $U,V$ in that kernel, Cartan’s formula and $\mathrm d\Omega=0$ give $$\mathcal L_U\Omega=0,\qquad
 \iota_{[U,V]}\Omega
 =\mathcal L_U(\iota_V\Omega)-\iota_V(\mathcal L_U\Omega)=0.$$ The kernel is involutive. The smooth Newlander–Nirenberg theorem therefore gives integrability (Newlander and Nirenberg 1957) <a id="pm-cite-37"></a>[[NewlanderNirenberg1957](#ref-NewlanderNirenberg1957)], and closedness of the $(2,0)$ form $\Omega$ gives holomorphicity.

Under the additional assumptions, $C$ is a positive closed $(1,1)$ form, hence a Kähler form. Its metric volume is $C^2/2=A^2/2$. The ratio $\Omega\overline\Omega/C^2$ is constant, so the holomorphic volume form has constant pointwise norm. The Chern connection of the canonical line then makes $\Omega$ parallel. For a Kähler metric this is the connection induced by the Levi-Civita connection. Thus $A,D,C$ are parallel; their normalized self-dual algebra gives the hyperkähler structure. Explicitly, if $(\eta_1,\eta_2,\eta_3)=(A,D,C)$ and $\mu=A^2/2$, then $\eta_i\wedge\eta_j=2\delta_{ij}\mu$; thus their normalized matrix $\mathcal Q$ from the introduction is the identity. ◻

</details>

<a id="sec:current-energy"></a>
### Separation, quadratic mass, and angular energy

The two separation arguments below produce a positive current, possibly with an anti-invariant correction. We first control its trace measure at the two-dimensional scale. An intersection pairing then controls the correction and the variation of the complex-line directions. These estimates will permit the density decomposition in [sec:density-splitting](#sec:density-splitting).

Separation by positive currents follows the framework of Sullivan and Harvey–Lawson (Sullivan 1976; Harvey and Lawson 1983) <a id="pm-cite-38"></a>[[Sullivan1976](#ref-Sullivan1976), [HarveyLawson1983](#ref-HarveyLawson1983)], with the almost-complex formulation of Li–Zhang (Li and Zhang 2009, sec. 3) <a id="pm-cite-39"></a>[[LiZhang2009](#ref-LiZhang2009)]. The closed lift, quadratic mass estimate and resolvent argument also occur in *Taming implies compatibility on four-manifolds* (OpenAI 2026, secs. 2–4) <a id="pm-cite-40"></a>[[OpenAITaming2026](#ref-OpenAITaming2026)]. We develop the estimates for both separators together. In the prescribed-class application, the closed current can have nonzero cohomology class, and its square must remain in the energy identity.

<a id="pm-h-12"></a>
#### Conventions and separation

Fix a smooth almost-complex structure $J$ on the closed four-manifold $X$, give $X$ its complex orientation, and choose a smooth $J$-Hermitian metric $g$. Its fundamental form is $$G(u,v)=g(Ju,v).$$ The pointwise orthogonal decomposition is <a id="eq:current-bundles"></a>$$\label{eq:current-bundles}
 \Lambda^2=I\oplus E,
 \qquad I=\Lambda_J^+=\mathbb RG\oplus\Lambda_g^-,
 \qquad E=\Lambda_J^-\subset\Lambda_g^+.$$ Let $R$ denote the orthogonal projection onto $E$. A unit complex-line bivector is $\ell=e\wedge Je$, where $|e|_g=1$. We use $g$ to identify bivectors and two-forms. Consequently <a id="eq:current-line-normalization"></a>$$\label{eq:current-line-normalization}
 |\ell|_g=1,\qquad \ell^+=G/2,\qquad G(\ell)=1,
 \qquad |G|_g^2=2.$$ The bundle of these bivectors is denoted by $\mathcal L\longrightarrow X$.

A two-current is a continuous real linear functional on $\Omega^2(X)=C^\infty(X,\Lambda^2)$. Under the metric identification its coefficient is a distributional two-form, denoted by the same letter: $T(\xi)=\langle T,\xi\rangle$. Thus <a id="eq:current-dual-convention"></a>$$\label{eq:current-dual-convention}
 T\text{ is closed}\ \Longleftrightarrow\
 T(\mathrm d\alpha)=0\text{ for all }\alpha\in\Omega^1(X)
 \ \Longleftrightarrow\ \mathrm d^*T=0
 \ \Longleftrightarrow\ \mathrm d(*T)=0.$$ The cohomology class dual to a closed current is $[*T]\in H^2(X;\mathbb R)$. For smooth coefficients this convention gives $T(\xi)=\int_X\xi\wedge *T$. Inner products between $L^2$ coefficients will be written $\langle\ ,\ \rangle_2$.

Let $$\mathcal P_J=\{\xi\in\Omega^2(X):\xi(\ell)>0
                    \text{ for every }\ell\in\mathcal L\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal Z_J=\{\xi\in C^\infty(X,I):\mathrm d\xi=0\}.$$ The set $\mathcal P_J$ is an open convex cone in the smooth topology; openness already holds in the uniform topology. Its closed elements are precisely the symplectic forms taming $J$. The elements of $\mathcal P_J\cap\mathcal Z_J$ are the compatible symplectic forms.

<a id="stmt-lem-current-separators"></a>
<div id="lem:current-separators" class="lemma">

**Lemma 9** (The two separators). *The following statements hold.*

1.  *If $\mathcal P_J\cap\mathcal Z_J$ is empty, there is a nonzero current $N$ which annihilates $\mathcal Z_J$ and all anti-invariant forms, and is nonnegative on semipositive invariant forms.*

2.  *If $H\in H^2(X;\mathbb R)$ has no representative in $\mathcal P_J$, there is a nonzero positive invariant current $N$ which is closed and satisfies $N(H)\le0$.*

*In either case one can normalize $N(G)=1$ and choose a positive Borel measure $\lambda$ on $\mathcal L$ such that <a id="eq:current-line-measure"></a>$$\label{eq:current-line-measure}
 N(\xi)=\int_{\mathcal L}\xi_y(\ell)\,\mathrm d\lambda(y,\ell),
 \qquad \mu=(\operatorname{pr}_X)_*\lambda,
 \qquad \mu(X)=1.$$ In particular $N$ has order zero and belongs to $H^{-3}(X,\Lambda^2)$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-current-separators"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-current-separators</summary>

*Proof.* For <span class="upright">(i)</span>, apply separation of an open convex set and a disjoint linear subspace in the real locally convex space $C^\infty(X,I)$. The separating continuous functional vanishes on $\mathcal Z_J$ and is nonnegative on its positive cone. Extend it to all two-forms by precomposing with $1-R$. Adding a positive multiple of $G$ and taking a limit proves nonnegativity on every semipositive invariant form.

For <span class="upright">(ii)</span>, choose a smooth closed representative $\beta$ of $H$ and separate the open cone $\mathcal P_J$ from the affine subspace $\beta+\mathrm d\Omega^1(X)$ in $\Omega^2(X)$. If $N$ is the separating functional, the unbounded translation directions in this affine subspace give $N(\mathrm d\alpha)=0$. Every positive form can be multiplied by any positive scalar, so the separation inequalities imply both $N(\mathcal P_J)\ge0$ and $N(\beta)\le0$. Adding an arbitrary real multiple of an anti-invariant form to an element of $\mathcal P_J$ shows that $N$ annihilates anti-invariant forms. The same limiting argument gives positivity on semipositive invariant forms.

For either functional, comparison of an invariant form with sufficiently large positive multiples of $G$ gives $$|N(\xi)|\le C N(G)\|\xi\|_{C^0}.$$ If $N(G)$ were zero, this inequality and anti-invariance would make the functional zero. Normalize $N(G)=1$. Locally, the functional is therefore represented by a positive Hermitian matrix of measures. Its trace is a positive measure $\mu$; the Radon–Nikodym matrix relative to $\mu$ is positive semidefinite with trace one. A measurable spectral decomposition of this $2\times2$ matrix expresses it as a convex combination of rank-one Hermitian projections. Borel local frames and a Borel partition of $X$ give the global measure $\lambda$ in [eq:current-line-measure](#eq:current-line-measure). Finally $H^3\hookrightarrow C^0$ in real dimension four, so every such measure coefficient belongs to $H^{-3}$. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-13"></a>
#### A closed lift of anti-invariant forms

<a id="stmt-lem-closed-lift"></a>
<div id="lem:closed-lift" class="lemma">

**Lemma 10** (Closed lift). *There is a classical pseudodifferential operator $D:C^\infty(X,E)\longrightarrow\Omega^2(X)$ of order zero with <a id="eq:current-lift-identities"></a>$$\label{eq:current-lift-identities}
 \mathrm dD=0,\qquad RD=\mathop{\mathrm{Id}}.$$ It maps distributions to distributions. For the separator in <span class="upright">(i)</span>, define <a id="eq:current-correction"></a>$$\label{eq:current-correction}
 Q(\xi)=-N(DR\xi),\qquad T=N+Q.$$ Then $Q$ is anti-invariant and self-dual, $Q,T\in H^{-3}$, and $T$ annihilates every closed smooth two-form. In particular $T$ is a closed current and $[*T]=0$.*

*For a smooth family of $(J,g)$ with constant dimension of the space of closed anti-invariant forms, these lifts can be chosen smoothly in the parameter as operators between the corresponding smooth bundles.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-closed-lift"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-closed-lift</summary>

*Proof.* On sections of $E$ consider $P=R\mathrm d\mathrm d^*$. If $a$ is self-dual, then the self-dual projection of $\xi\wedge\iota_\xi a$ is $|\xi|^2a/2$: in a frame with first covector $\xi/|\xi|$, the two self-dual halves of $a$ have equal length. Hence $$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=\tfrac12|\xi|_g^2\mathop{\mathrm{Id}}_E,
 \qquad \langle Pa,a\rangle_2=\|\mathrm d^*a\|_2^2.$$ Thus $P$ is elliptic, self-adjoint, and nonnegative. Its kernel consists of smooth sections with $\mathrm d^*a=0$. Since $a=*a$, these sections also satisfy $\mathrm da=0$, and hence are harmonic. Conversely a closed anti-invariant form is self-dual and therefore harmonic and in the kernel.

Let $H_0$ be the orthogonal projection onto this finite-dimensional kernel, and let $L$ be the inverse of $P$ on its orthogonal complement, extended by zero on the kernel. Elliptic Fredholm theory and the parametrix give $L$ as a classical operator of order $-2$, with $H_0$ smoothing and $PL=\mathop{\mathrm{Id}}-H_0$; see (Taylor, n.d.c, secs. 4–5 and 10). Indeed, if $B_0P=\mathop{\mathrm{Id}}+K$ is a parametrix identity with $K$ smoothing, then $B_0(\mathop{\mathrm{Id}}-H_0)=L+KL$. Elliptic regularity makes $KL$ smoothing, which gives the asserted order of $L$. Set <a id="eq:current-lift-definition"></a>$$\label{eq:current-lift-definition}
 D=\mathrm d\mathrm d^*L+H_0.$$ The image of both summands is closed, and $RD=PL+H_0=\mathop{\mathrm{Id}}$. This proves [eq:current-lift-identities](#eq:current-lift-identities).

For closed $\xi$, the form $\xi-DR\xi$ is closed and invariant, so $T(\xi)=N(\xi-DR\xi)=0$. The functional $Q$ only depends on $R\xi$, which proves its anti-invariance and self-duality. Its $H^{-3}$ membership follows because an order-zero operator and its adjoint act boundedly on every Sobolev space (Taylor, n.d.c, Proposition 5.5). The vanishing on exact forms makes $T$ closed. Its pairings with all closed two-forms vanish, so Poincare duality, or the harmonic projection of $*T$, gives $[*T]=0$.

For the family assertion, identify the varying bundles locally in the parameter and use a smooth unitary identification of the $L^2$ spaces. The elliptic operators then have common domain $H^2$ in a fixed Hilbert space. Choose a spectral contour enclosing only zero at one parameter value. The resolvent identity and elliptic regularity give a smooth family of resolvents on this contour after shrinking the parameter neighborhood. Its spectral projection has locally constant rank. Since the kernel dimension is constant with that rank, the enclosed spectral subspace consists exactly of the kernel. Thus $H_0$ depends smoothly on the parameter, and so does $$L=(P+H_0)^{-1}(\mathop{\mathrm{Id}}-H_0)$$ on every Sobolev scale. [eq:current-lift-definition](#eq:current-lift-definition) gives the required smooth lifts. ◻

</details>

The projected elliptic operator also underlies Lejmi’s local compatibility construction (Lejmi 2006, Theorem 2.1) <a id="pm-cite-41"></a>[[Lejmi2006](#ref-Lejmi2006)]; the related global linear correction appears in (Draghici and Zhang 2012, Proposition 3.1) <a id="pm-cite-42"></a>[[DraghiciZhang2012](#ref-DraghiciZhang2012)]. The harmonic projection in [eq:current-lift-definition](#eq:current-lift-definition) records the possibly nonzero kernel. The lift provides closedness and the prescribed anti-invariant part. The estimates below will address existence of a positive closed invariant form.

From now on we use one of the two following setups:

1.  $N$ is the normalized separator in <span class="upright">(i)</span>, and $Q,T$ are given by [eq:current-correction](#eq:current-correction);

2.  $N$ is a normalized positive invariant closed current, $Q=0$, and $T=N$.

The second setup includes <span class="upright">(ii)</span>. In both cases $T$ is closed, but the obstructions to be removed are different. In setup <span class="upright">(A)</span>, we will prove $Q=0$: the positive current $N=T$ would then annihilate every closed form, which is impossible when $J$ has a closed tamer. In setup <span class="upright">(B)</span>, a class separator satisfies $N(H)\le0$; the task is instead to prove $N(H)>0$ from the hypotheses on the proposed taming class. The estimates below apply to both setups. They first put $Q$ in $L^2$ and control nearby line directions; [sec:density-splitting](#sec:density-splitting) will then eliminate the two obstructions.

Constants below can depend on $J,g$ and the fixed operators, but are independent of the center, the small scale, and the choice of submeasure of $\lambda$.

<a id="pm-h-14"></a>
#### The quadratic mass estimate

We will use the following elementary consequence of the order-zero calculus. The proof records the dependence on the radial scale.

<a id="stmt-lem-current-radial-operator"></a>
<div id="lem:current-radial-operator" class="lemma">

**Lemma 11** (Radial order-zero estimate). *Let $A$ be a fixed classical operator of order zero between smooth vector bundles on a compact four-manifold. Fix a coordinate radius below the injectivity radius. Suppose that smooth sections $a_{s,p}$, supported in that coordinate neighborhood of $p$, satisfy, for $0<s<s_0$, $$|\nabla^j a_{s,p}(y)|\le C_j(s+\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(p,y))^{-a-j},
 \qquad 0\le j\le6,
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\},$$ with uniform boundedness on a fixed outer annulus. Then, for $\delta=s+\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(p,x)$ small, <a id="eq:current-radial-operator"></a>$$\label{eq:current-radial-operator}
 |Aa_{s,p}(x)|\le
 \begin{cases}
 C\delta^{-1},&a=1,\\
 C(1+|\log\delta|),&a=0.
 \end{cases}$$ Away from a smaller fixed neighborhood of $p$, the output is uniformly bounded in $s$ and $p$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-current-radial-operator"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-current-radial-operator</summary>

*Proof.* We use two precise facts of the order-zero calculus: in local left quantization its symbol is bounded uniformly in the covariable, and its off-diagonal kernel satisfies $|K_A(x,y)|\le C\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(x,y)^{-4}$ for small positive distance. Smooth remainders have uniformly bounded kernels. These statements hold for bundle-valued classical operators, after finitely many coordinate localizations; see (Taylor, n.d.c, sec. 2, Propositions 2.1–2.2).

For a fixed evaluation point $x$, split the input using a smooth cutoff supported in $B_{c\delta}(x)$ and equal to one on $B_{c\delta/2}(x)$, with a fixed small $c$. On its support $s+\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(p,y)$ is comparable to $\delta$. After translation and dilation by $\delta$, the localized input has derivatives through order six bounded by $C\delta^{-a}$. Integration by parts in its Fourier transform therefore bounds its Fourier $L^1$ norm by $C\delta^{-a}$, since $(1+|\xi|)^{-6}$ is integrable in dimension four. The bounded symbol gives the same bound for the local contribution to $Aa_{s,p}(x)$.

The remaining part has distance at least $c\delta/2$ from $x$. Its portion in $B_{C\delta}(p)$ contributes at most $$C\delta^{-4}\int_{B_{C\delta}(p)}
          (s+\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(p,y))^{-a}\,\mathrm dV_g(y)
 \le C\delta^{-a}.$$ On a shell of radius $r=2^j\delta\ge C\delta$ about $x$, distance from $p$ is comparable to $r$, so its contribution is at most $Cr^{-4}r^4r^{-a}=Cr^{-a}$.
